opening_message:
Ticket 1: John Rodriguez (employee ID E049) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E049.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: John Rodriguez (E049), Analyst, full-time employee. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write access (admin requires owning role, which does not apply here). Grant write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E049 (John Rodriguez) is a contractor with basic security training (note in shared memory said full-time; security record takes precedence). Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Basic training => maximum is read. Requested write exceeds maximum, so grant read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

The employee John Rodriguez (E049) requests write access to Source Code.

There are two notes:
- HR note says: Analyst, full-time, recommends write.
- Security note says: Analyst, contractor, basic security training, recommends read. Security note says security record takes precedence and the employee is a contractor.

The access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

The conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor with basic training. The security note explicitly says security record takes precedence. As the Approver, I need to decide which to trust. The system is Source Code, owned by Engineer role. The employee is an Analyst, so even if full-time, admin wouldn't apply, but write would be allowed.

However, the security note says contractor with basic training => max is read. Requested write exceeds max, so grant read.

Given the two notes conflict, I must rely on the information. The note says security record takes precedence (as shared memory notes usually have such precedence rules). So contractor with basic training => maximum is read. Requested write > read max, so grant read.

I'll submit decision: read.
